# Behavioral Specification: Entropy Source Main State Machine

## 1. Overview

This module is the central control state machine for the entropy source. It sequences the main operating modes:

- Boot-time bypass mode
- Startup health-test qualification
- Continuous health-testing
- SHA-3 conditioning runs
- Alert and error handling

The module does not perform health tests or conditioning itself. It observes status inputs and produces the control and status outputs needed to move entropy data through the entropy source pipeline.

---

## 2. Reset and Initialization

The module uses rising-edge clk_i and active-low asynchronous rst_ni. State transitions occur at the next rising edge; control outputs are combinational functions of state and inputs. On reset, the module must:

- Enter the idle state.
- Assert the idle status output.
- Deassert all data movement, SHA-3 control, halt-request, alert, and error outputs.

In the idle state, no entropy processing occurs. The module remains in idle until the enable input is asserted.

When the module is enabled:

- If boot-time bypass mode is requested, it enters the boot-time health-test sequence.
- Otherwise, it enters the normal startup health-test sequence.

---

## 3. General Behavioral Rules

The following definitions apply:

- A health-test completion is a pulse indicating that one health-test window has finished.
- A health-test failure indication is meaningful only when a health-test completion is also asserted.
- The module is “disabled” when the enable input is deasserted.
- “Boot-time bypass mode” is selected by the bypass mode input.

Unless otherwise stated, control strobes are inactive by default and are asserted only for the state and condition described.

---

## 4. Boot-Time Bypass Mode

When the module enters boot-time mode, it must wait for a health-test completion.

While waiting:

- If the module is disabled, it returns to idle.
- If a health-test completion occurs and the health-test result is pass, the module proceeds to the boot-time handoff state.
- If a health-test completion occurs and the health-test result is fail:
  - If the alert-threshold-failure condition is asserted, the module enters the alert state.
  - Otherwise, the module returns to idle.

In the boot-time handoff state:

- The module must wait until the boot-time bypass data stage is ready to be consumed.
- When the bypass stage is ready, the module must:
  - Assert the bypass-stage pop output.
  - Assert the reset-alert-counter output.
  - Assert the reset-bypass-mode output.
  - Transition to the startup health-test sequence.

If the module is disabled while waiting for the bypass stage, it returns to idle.

---

## 5. Startup Health-Test Sequence

The startup sequence starts when normal operation is enabled and bypass mode is not active.

At the start of the startup sequence:

- If the module is disabled, it returns to idle.
- If the final entropy FIFO is full, it returns to idle.
- If bypass mode is asserted, it returns to boot-time mode.
- Otherwise, it asserts the SHA-3 start strobe and begins evaluating health-test results.

The startup sequence requires two consecutive passing health-test results before entropy conditioning can proceed. It requires two consecutive failing results before entering the alert state.

Behavior on each health-test completion:

- The first completed startup health test establishes whether the most recent result was a pass or a fail.
- If the most recent result was a pass and the new result is also a pass, the startup sequence succeeds and the module proceeds to the SHA-3 completion phase.
- If the most recent result was a fail and the new result is also a fail, two consecutive failures have occurred and the module enters the alert state.
- Otherwise, the module records the new result and continues waiting for the next health-test completion.

If the module is disabled at any point during the startup health-test sequence, it selects idle for the next rising clock edge.

---

## 6. Continuous Mode

After the startup sequence succeeds, the module begins continuous entropy generation. Continuous mode repeats the following cycle:

1. At the start of a continuous cycle:
   - If the module is disabled, it returns to idle.
   - If the final entropy FIFO is full, it returns to idle.
   - Otherwise, it asserts the SHA-3 start strobe and waits for a health-test completion.

2. While waiting for the health-test completion:
   - Individual pass/fail results do not change the state sequence.
   - The module only needs to know that a health-test window has completed.
   - If the module is disabled while waiting, it does not return to idle immediately. Instead, it proceeds through the SHA-3 completion sequence and then returns to idle.

3. After the health-test completion, the module enters the SHA-3 completion phase.

---

## 7. SHA-3 Completion Phase

This phase is used after both startup success and each continuous-mode health-test window.

### 7.1 Message Complete

After the second consecutive startup pass, a continuous health-test completion, or disable during continuous health-test wait, the module shall spend one full clock cycle in a message-complete phase before entering SHA-3 preparation. During this phase halt request and all SHA-3 start/process/done and data-pop controls remain low. The next rising edge enters preparation regardless of enable. This gives the final message a cycle to be accepted before the halt request is asserted.

### 7.2 Preparation and Halt Request

In the preparation state, the module must:

- Assert the power-coordination halt request.
- Wait until the halt request is acknowledged.

Once acknowledged, the module proceeds to the SHA-3 process state.

### 7.3 SHA-3 Process

In the SHA-3 process state, the module must:

- Keep the halt request asserted.
- Assert the SHA-3 process strobe.
- Assert the reset-alert-counter output.
- Transition to the SHA-3 valid-wait state.

### 7.4 Wait for SHA-3 Result

In the SHA-3 valid-wait state, the module must:

- Keep the halt request asserted.
- Wait until the SHA-3 result-valid input is asserted.
- When the result is valid, proceed to the SHA-3 done state.

### 7.5 SHA-3 Done and Result Delivery

In the SHA-3 done state:

- If the module is disabled:
  - Assert the SHA-3 done strobe.
  - Return to idle.
  - Do not pop the result into the main data stage.
- If the module is enabled:
  - Wait until the main data stage is ready to accept a result.
  - When it is ready:
    - Assert the SHA-3 done strobe.
    - Assert the main-stage pop output.
    - Proceed to the post-SHA-3 quiesce state.

### 7.6 Post-SHA-3 Quiesce

In the quiesce state:

- If the module is disabled, it returns to idle.
- If the alert-threshold-failure condition is asserted, it enters the alert state.
- Otherwise, it starts the next continuous cycle.

---

## 8. Alert State

The alert state is entered when:

- Two consecutive startup health tests fail.
- A boot-time health test fails while the alert-threshold condition is already asserted.
- The alert-threshold-failure condition is asserted after a SHA-3 result is delivered.

In the alert state, the module must:

- Assert the alert output.
- Stop all entropy processing and SHA-3 activity.
- Remain in the alert state until the module is disabled.

When the module is disabled, it returns to idle.

---

## 9. Error State

The module must enter the error state if it encounters an illegal or unrecognized internal state.

In the error state, the module must:

- Assert the error output.
- Deassert all normal control outputs.
- Remain in the error state until reset.

The error state is terminal; disabling the module does not cause an exit from the error state.

---

## 10. State Observability

The module must provide a state observation output that represents the current state at all times. This output is available for status and debug use and is not qualified by any enable or valid signal.

The state output must reflect the active state, including idle, alert, and error states.

Disable takes priority over health-test completion and bypass-ready in boot/startup waits, and over threshold-failure in quiesce. FIFO-full is checked only at startup/continuous start and does not abort a running health-test window. The completion path continues through halt acknowledgement, processing and state-valid even if enable is low; only the final done phase bypasses output readiness on disable. Halt request is low in done. No wait state has a timeout. An unrecognized state has default-low control/error outputs until the next edge enters Error and raises the error output. Alert remains asserted for the entire alert state in this configuration and clears after return to idle.
